text:
Aisha: quick follow-up on the rollout metadata RFC — I want to propose a tighter surface for release-level pinning. instead of separate fields spread across `pin`, `lease`, `affinity_hint`, i propose a single canonical object encoded as flattened fields: `release_affinity`, `compat_version`, `cohort` and an optional `soft_ttl`.

Aisha: rough sketch: `release_affinity` = one of ["hard", "soft", "prefer"]; `compat_version` = semver-ish string or content-hash; `cohort` = freeform small label for segmented rollouts; `soft_ttl` = ISO duration to indicate client-side expiry.

Tom: +1 to flattening. avoids clients having to plumb multiple fallbacks. question: how do we signal cross-compat fallthroughs? e.g., model A v2 can accept v3 payloads?

Priya: we discussed `compat_buckets` in the RFC but it felt heavy. maybe `compat_version` can be a comma list of accepted versions, or we add `compat_policy` enum {"strict","allow-minor","fallback"}.

Jordi: +1 for `compat_policy`. we should also include a machine-parseable provenance tag for telemetry: `binding_source` (e.g., "release", "tenant-override", "canary") so we can attribute latency/cost deltas to how the model was pinned.

Aisha: good point. adding `binding_source` is lightweight. also want to avoid exploding the runtime surface — runtime should only read `binding_source`, `release_affinity`, `compat_policy`, `compat_version` and `cohort`. everything else stays as metadata for ops.

Tom: migration concern: older clients and control plane send `pin` object. we need a deterministic mapping doc: `pin.mode="hard" -> release_affinity="hard"`, `pin.alias -> cohort`, legacy `lease_ttl` -> `soft_ttl` but only if `lease_kind=soft`. do we want the control plane to auto-populate both old and new fields for a transitional period?

Priya: I'd prefer the control plane populate both for 3 months and emit a deprecation metric `rollout.metadata.legacy_field_used`. then flip a guard at 90 days. ops will need an alert if legacy usage > 1% for a tenant.

Jordi: runtime impact: reading an extra few flattened fields is cheap. bigger worry is storage bloat in rollout history. recommend we normalize storage: store canonicalized JSON and keep legacy original as compressed log in S3 for audit. UI/clients always read canonicalized view.

Tom: compatibility matrices for multi-variant routing? e.g., candidate variant groups where affinity is "prefer" but not hard. we need to decide evaluation order: affinity -> compat_policy -> fallback list. Should be deterministic.

Aisha: propose this order: 1) hard affinity exact match -> serve. 2) compat_policy allow-minor -> try compatible variants by compat_version ordering. 3) prefer -> if preferred not available, fall back to release pool. 4) fallback -> use fallback list or default model. Documented and unit-tested in resolver.

Priya: unit test matrix request: include tenant overrides, burst capacity fallback, and quantized model variants. we should add a property `variant_affinity_weight` (0-100) for soft preferences that router can use for probabilistic routing.

Jordi: weight is ok but keep it optional. we must clamp weights in runtime and avoid split-by-weight for tiny qps tenants. add runtime guard: if tenant_qps < 10, ignore weights and use deterministic fallback.

Aisha: ops/observability: we will attach these fields to every decision trace and include `binding_source` in logs. add a new alert if average latency for cohorts deviates > 20% vs baseline for 30m.

Tom: telemetry schema: `rollout.bind`, `rollout.binding_source`, `rollout.cohort`, `rollout.compat_policy`, `rollout.compat_version`, `rollout.affinity`. these should be tags not free text. enforce allowed enums at ingestion.

Priya: docs: update the client contract page and the console UI to show the canon fields. include a migration guide with mapping table and timeline.

ops-bot: schema-lint: checked 1716504321_release_affinity_schema.yaml -> OK.

Aisha: action items: 
- Priya to draft migration plan & deprecation metric (ETA 48h)
- Tom to add resolver ordering tests + weight guard (ETA 72h)
- Jordi to propose storage normalization & retention for legacy blobs (ETA 72h)
- Aisha to update RFC + add canonical json example and telemetry keys (ETA 24h)

Tom: one more thought — clients that pin by label (human friendly names) will need a stable alias mapping. recommend we add `alias_id` (opaque id) to canonical view so names can change but alias_id stays stable.

Aisha: agree. add `alias_id` optional. good catch.

Priya: ok i'm on the migration plan. will include deprecation alert thresholds.

Jordi: i'll send a short PR for normalized storage layout and retention rules.

Aisha: thanks everyone. i'll publish the RFC follow-up and schedule a 30m sync if needed.

Tom: :thumbsup:

Priya: :rocket:
